name: Neptune Psychology
description: Defines Neptune's psychological needs, sensitivities, protective strategies, regulation needs, blind spots, and integration markers.

coreNeed.definition: Sufficient openness to feeling, image, atmosphere, and symbolic meaning without losing the ability to distinguish self, other, fact, image, and interpretation.

coreMotivation.definition: Enter forms of contact that exceed narrow literal, individual, or controlled experience.

coreSensitivity.definition: Heightened responsiveness to mood, tone, rhythm, image, and unspoken context.
Heightened responsiveness to pain, vulnerability, exclusion, or unmet need.
Heightened responsiveness to metaphor, association, dream, image, and nonliteral meaning.
Heightened responsiveness to the degree of separation or permeability between self, other, environment, and experience.

coreFearPatterns.definition: Fear that literal reality is empty, disconnected, or spiritually barren.
Fear of isolation from shared feeling, purpose, imagination, or collective experience.
Fear that clear separation, limitation, or refusal will be emotionally unbearable.
Fear that reality will not sustain an ideal, image, hope, or sensed possibility.

protectiveStrategies.definition: Preserve meaning or hope by organizing perception around an ideal image.
Assign internal image, longing, or fear outward when distinction is insufficient.
Move into image, fantasy, atmosphere, or altered attention to reduce contact with immediate difficulty.
Reduce personal boundary or preference in order to preserve connection, compassion, or idealized unity.
Keep conditions ambiguous when clearer distinction threatens an image, bond, or hope.

blindSpots: Confusing empathy with accurate knowledge of another person
Confusing symbolic meaning with literal prediction

regulationNeeds.definition: Remain open while preserving a clear channel, limit, or threshold.
Compare image, feeling, intuition, and ideal with observable conditions.
Choose what enters attention rather than receiving every signal equally.
Allow symbolic meaning without treating it as factual certainty.
Remain responsive to suffering without surrendering all personal choice or capacity.

healthyPsychologicalFunctions: Receive subtle information without assuming certainty
Let symbolic meaning coexist with literal reality
Allow inspiration to become concrete expression
Recognize atmosphere without treating it as proof
Soften boundaries while preserving consent and agency
integrationMarkers: Can tolerate disillusionment without abandoning meaning
Can maintain compassion and boundaries together
Can identify whether a perception is literal, symbolic, emotional, or imaginal
Can remain inspired after an ideal becomes more realistic
Can receive another person's pain without assuming ownership of it
Can surrender control without surrendering responsibility
Can let ambiguity remain open without losing all discernment
Can move between receptivity and containment
reflectionComponents: What is actually crossing this boundary?
Which part of this perception is literal, symbolic, emotional, or imagined?
Where would more receptivity help, and where would more distinction help?
Is this surrender chosen or compelled?
What observable reality supports this ideal?
Can compassion remain present without self-erasure?
psychologyConstraints: Psychology may qualify Neptunian expression but may not diagnose dissociation, addiction, delusion, or trauma.
No protective strategy may be treated as universally active.
No internal motive may be inferred from Neptune alone.
Empathy must not be equated with mind reading.
Developmental language must reference the global development blueprint.

provenance.sourcePolicy: Component-only planetary vocabulary. Psychology and development qualify expression but do not redefine Neptune.
